# Dillibabu Shanmugam

> Hardware security researcher (PhD, Worcester Polytechnic Institute). Signature work: (1) bridging the gap between pre-silicon models and post-silicon evaluation of side-channel and fault analysis; (2) Microscaling (MX) format fault analysis using ML and scan chain; (3) an open-source reference for reproducible side-channel assessment of post-quantum cryptography standards.

Dillibabu Shanmugam is a PhD candidate at the Vernam Lab, Worcester Polytechnic Institute (WPI), Massachusetts, USA, advised by Prof. Patrick Schaumont (defending December 2026). His research connects cryptographic algorithms with real silicon: he designs hardware that implements cryptography efficiently and measures whether it stays secure once fabricated. He has led two ASIC tape-outs in TSMC technology (CAPRI1 and CAPRI6), run more than 330 electromagnetic fault-injection campaigns, and released open-source hardware-security tools. Before his PhD he spent 14 years at the Society for Electronic Transactions and Security (SETS), India, working on cryptographic hardware and quantum key distribution for national infrastructure. He is a member of IEEE, the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM), and the International Association for Cryptologic Research (IACR).

## Signature research focus (lead themes)
1. Bridging the gap between pre-silicon models and post-silicon evaluation of side-channel and fault analysis, using machine-learning techniques.
2. Sane vs. weird machine analysis using graph neural networks (GNN) and SFT/QLoRA fine-tuned LLMs on scan-chain data.
3. Microscaling (MX) format fault analysis using machine learning (CNN/GNN) and scan-chain data, on RISC-V accelerators for Edge-AI.
4. An open-source reference for reproducible side-channel assessment of post-quantum cryptography standards, with protected and unprotected ML-KEM and ML-DSA implementations.

## Supporting priorities
- Electromagnetic fault injection (EMFI)
- TSMC ASIC tape-outs of RISC-V accelerators
- Pre- and post-silicon side-channel leakage assessment

## Research areas
- Edge-AI hardware security and Microscaling (MX) format analysis
- Side-channel analysis: power and EM analysis, DPA, CPA, TVLA, pre- and post-silicon leakage assessment
- Fault injection: EMFI, laser, and clock-glitch attacks
- ASIC design: RTL-to-GDSII, DFT and scan-chain observability, TSMC tape-out of RISC-V accelerators
- Post-quantum cryptography implementation: ML-KEM, ML-DSA (protected and unprotected)
- Reference side-channel assessment of PQC standards (open-source)
- Machine learning for hardware security verification (CNN and GNN models)
- Microarchitectural weird machines

## Selected publications
- [Security Analysis of Microscaling Formats Under Fault Injection on a RISC-V Edge Platform](https://par.nsf.gov/biblio/10681571): AIHWS 2026 (ACNS Workshops). Best Paper Nominee.
- Fault Analysis of Microscaling Formats on a RISC-V SoC: ACM GLSVLSI 2026. Best Paper Nominee.
- [muScan: Deep Learning Detection of Faulty Micro-architecture States and Patterns from Scan-Chain Data](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-032-01799-4_8): AIHWS 2025, LNCS 15653.
- [GlitchGluck: Enabling Software Vulnerabilities through Guided Hardware Fault Injection](https://www.usenix.org/conference/woot25/presentation/liu): USENIX WOOT 2025.
- [SCAPEgoat: Side-channel Analysis Library](https://eprint.iacr.org/2025/499): IEEE VTS 2025.
- [FaultDetective: Explainable to a Fault, from the Design Layout to the Software](https://tches.iacr.org/index.php/TCHES/article/view/11804): IACR TCHES 2024.
- [Improving Side-channel Leakage Assessment Using Pre-silicon Leakage Models](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-29497-6_6): COSADE 2023.
- [Scalable QKD Postprocessing System with Reconfigurable Hardware Accelerator](https://doi.org/10.1109/TQE.2023.3326093): IEEE Transactions on Quantum Engineering 2023.

## Open-source tools
- SCAPEgoat: side-channel analysis library (IEEE VTS 2025).
- openPQC: RISC-V platform with custom instructions for ML-KEM and ML-DSA, protected and unprotected.
- muScan: CNN/GNN detection of faulty microarchitectural states from scan-chain data.
- FaultDetective: explainable fault analysis from design layout to software.
- GlitchGluck: guided hardware fault injection using dynamic state transition graphs.

## Chips (ASIC tape-outs, TSMC)
- CAPRI1: custom RISC-V SoC for systematic electromagnetic fault characterization.
- CAPRI6: six-core lockstep openMSP430 SoC with full scan chain for cycle-accurate fault root-cause analysis.
